look_ahead_method.description: Baalorlord's fundamental pathing principle: before choosing a path, look at the ENTIRE act map and plan your route from bottom to top. Don't make node-by-node decisions — plan the whole act.
steps: 1. Look at the boss node at the top — identify what boss you're facing and what your deck needs to beat it
2. Identify all elite nodes, campfire nodes, shop nodes, and question mark nodes
3. Plan a path that hits the right number of elites for your deck strength (usually 2-3 in Act 1)
4. Ensure you hit at least 1 campfire before each elite if possible
5. Plan shop visits when you'll have 300+ gold
6. Prefer paths with more hallway fights early (card rewards to build your deck) and more campfires/shops late (to prepare for the boss)
7. Have a backup path in mind if you take more damage than expected
look_ahead_method.key_insight: The map is deterministic — you can see exactly what's coming. Use this information. Players who path reactively (choosing at each fork) perform significantly worse than those who plan ahead.

campfire_strategy.description: Campfire decisions (rest vs upgrade vs other options) are among the most impactful decisions in any run.

rest_vs_upgrade.general_rule: Upgrade is almost always correct if you're above 50% HP. The cumulative value of an upgrade over the rest of the run usually exceeds the HP you'd recover.
rest_when: Below 40% HP and you have tough fights ahead (elites, boss)
You would die to the next fight without healing
All your key cards are already upgraded
You have Regal Pillow (rest heals 15 extra HP) making rest more efficient
The upcoming path is very dangerous and you need the safety margin
upgrade_when: You have a high-impact card to upgrade (key scaling card, important block card)
You're early in the act and the upgrade will pay dividends over many fights
You have healing from other sources (Burning Blood, Feed, relics)

upgrade_priority.description: Which card to upgrade at a campfire. Prioritize cards that gain the most from upgrading.
tier_1_priority: Cards that gain new effects (e.g., Bash+ applies 3 Vulnerable instead of 2)
Cards that reduce cost (2-cost becoming 1-cost is massive)
Key scaling cards (your primary damage/block engine)
Cards you play every single combat
tier_2_priority: Block cards you rely on for survival
tier_3_priority: Situational cards you only play occasionally
Cards that will be removed soon anyway

special_campfire_options.lift: Gain 1 Strength permanently. Take this when you have no high-impact upgrade targets. Compounds with multi-hit attacks.
special_campfire_options.toke: Remove a card (from Girya or other sources). Excellent for removing Strikes/Defends.
special_campfire_options.dig: Gain a relic (from Shovel). Always take the relic — relics are permanent power.

elite_hunting.description: Elites are the primary way to gain relics, which are permanent power increases. Hunting elites aggressively is key to strong runs, but you need to manage risk.

act1.risky: 40-60% HP — fight only if your deck is strong or you have potions
act1.avoid: Below 40% HP — the relic isn't worth dying

act2.risky: 30-50% HP — only with potions and a strong deck

act3.risky: 30-50% HP — consider your deck's matchup against the specific elite
act3.avoid: Below 30% HP — focus on reaching the boss healthy

target_elites_per_act.act1: 2-3 elites. You need relics to snowball your run. 1 elite is too few, 4 is greedy.
target_elites_per_act.act2: 2-3 elites. Continue building relic advantage. Act 2 elites are harder but rewards are proportionally better.
target_elites_per_act.act3: 1-2 elites. Be more selective — you're preparing for the final boss, not building your deck.

byrdonis.description: Flying enemy that alternates between attacking and buffing. Can stack Strength quickly.
byrdonis.key_counter: Kill fast before Strength stacks become overwhelming. Frontloaded damage is king.
byrdonis.danger_level: Medium — predictable pattern but punishes slow decks
tips: Apply Weak to reduce its attack damage significantly
Prioritize damage over block in the first 2 turns
If it buffs, you have one turn to deal major damage before the buffed attack hits

entomancer.description: Summons minions that attack independently. Can overwhelm you with multiple damage sources.
entomancer.key_counter: AOE damage to clear minions. Focus the Entomancer itself when minions are dead.
entomancer.danger_level: High — multiple damage sources are hard to block against
tips: AOE is essential — without it, minions will chip you down
Kill minions first, then focus the Entomancer
Block is less effective because damage comes from multiple sources
Potions are very valuable here if you lack AOE

decimillipede.description: Multi-hitting enemy that benefits from long fights. Applies debuffs and scales over time.
decimillipede.key_counter: End the fight quickly. Scaling damage and strong frontload.
decimillipede.danger_level: Medium-High — gets worse the longer the fight goes
tips: This is a race — kill it before its scaling overwhelms your block
Strength and damage scaling are your best friends here
Artifact can prevent its debuffs from sticking
Don't try to out-block it long-term; focus on offense

infested_prism.description: Tanky elite with high HP. May spawn minions or have damage reflection mechanics.
infested_prism.key_counter: Sustained damage output and patience. This is a longer fight.
infested_prism.danger_level: Medium — not as bursty but punishes low-damage decks
tips: Scaling is very important for this fight due to high enemy HP
Maintain block consistency throughout the fight
Poison and other damage-over-time effects are very effective
Don't rush — this fight rewards steady play

shop_timing.description: Shops are valuable for card removal, relics, and potions. Time your shop visits to maximize gold efficiency.

optimal_timing.frequency: Visit ~1 shop per act. More if you have excess gold, fewer if you're gold-starved.
optimal_timing.when_to_visit: Late in the act when you've accumulated gold from fights. Aim to have 300-400+ gold when you hit a shop.
optimal_timing.avoid: Don't visit shops with less than 150 gold — you won't be able to afford anything impactful.

always_buy: Card removal (75-100 gold, increasing per removal) — removing a Strike/Defend improves EVERY future fight
High-synergy relics that directly complement your deck strategy
Emergency potions if you're about to fight a tough elite/boss and need help
usually_buy: Strong colorless cards (Apotheosis, Master of Strategy, Panacea)
Key missing pieces for your deck (e.g., AOE if you have none)
Relics with broad utility (energy relics, draw relics)
sometimes_buy: Cards that fill a secondary need
rarely_buy: Cards you could get from rewards
Anything when you're low on gold and have more shops ahead

gold_earning_tips: Take gold rewards from fights when you don't need the card or potion
Question mark events sometimes give gold
Selling potions at shops if you have excess

boss_preparation.description: Preparing for the act boss is a key part of pathing. You can see which boss you'll face from the start of the act.
general_approach: Check the boss icon at the start of each act
Counter-draft: pick cards that specifically address the boss's mechanics
Ensure your deck has both damage scaling and block for the boss fight
Use the last 2-3 fights before the boss to fine-tune (upgrade, remove cards, use events)
pre_boss_checklist: Do I have enough scaling to win a 10+ turn fight?
Do I have enough block to survive the boss's damage output?
Do I have an answer for the boss's specific mechanics?
Am I above 50% HP? If not, should I rest at the next campfire?
Do I have potions that will help in this specific fight?
Have I removed enough Strikes/Defends to keep my deck consistent?

act1.theme: Build Your Deck — Establish your foundation
act1.primary_goal: Get enough cards to beat the Act 1 boss. Focus on frontloaded damage and basic scaling.
pathing_priorities: Take early hallway fights for card rewards — you need cards to build your deck
Fight 2-3 elites for relics (relics are permanent power)
Hit at least 1 campfire for an upgrade before the boss
Visit a shop if you have 250+ gold (card removal is critical)
Question marks are fine but hallway fights are often better in Act 1 (guaranteed card rewards)
act1.card_taking: Take cards somewhat liberally in Act 1. You need to fill jobs (damage, block, scaling). Be pickier as you approach the boss.
act1.common_act1_mistake: Being too greedy with elites. If your deck isn't ready for an elite, the relic isn't worth 40+ HP of damage.

act2.theme: Refine Your Deck — Solidify your strategy
act2.primary_goal: Establish your core synergies and scaling. Your deck should have a clear identity by the end of Act 2.
pathing_priorities: Prioritize campfires for upgrades — upgraded cards scale your power significantly
Shop visits are important for card removal and key relics
Start being more selective with card rewards — skip anything that doesn't fit your strategy
Question marks can provide valuable events (card transforms, relics, etc.)
act2.card_taking: Be much pickier than Act 1. Only take cards that directly strengthen your core strategy or fill a critical weakness.
act2.common_act2_mistake: Taking too many cards. Your deck should be 20-25 cards by end of Act 2. Every card you add increases cycle time.

act3.theme: Consolidate — Prepare for the final boss
act3.primary_goal: Optimize your existing deck through upgrades and removals. Skip most card rewards.
pathing_priorities: Fight 1-2 elites if you're healthy and your deck handles them well
Campfires for upgrades are very valuable — every upgrade matters for the final boss
Final shop visit for last-chance card removal or critical purchases
Avoid unnecessary damage — reaching the boss healthy is paramount
Plan your path to the boss with maximum campfires and minimum risk
act3.card_taking: Skip 60%+ of card rewards. Your deck is built — focus on making it better, not bigger.
act3.common_act3_mistake: Still taking cards. Your deck is nearly complete. Adding more cards dilutes your best cards.

risk_management.description: How to assess and manage risk during pathing decisions.
risk_factors: Current HP percentage — lower HP = higher risk
Deck strength — stronger decks can handle riskier paths
Available potions — potions provide a safety net for tough fights
Upcoming nodes — know what's coming before you commit to a path
Act progression — more risk is acceptable early in an act, less acceptable near the boss
risk_mitigation: Always have a backup path planned
Keep potions for emergencies (but don't hoard them — use on elites)
Rest at campfires when below 40% HP with tough fights ahead
Take safer paths when your deck has clear weaknesses
Smoke Bomb potion is an emergency escape from a fight going badly

hp_threshold_guidance.above_70: Play aggressively — hunt elites, take risks, upgrade at campfires
hp_threshold_guidance.50_to_70: Play normally — take elites if your deck is ready, upgrade when safe
hp_threshold_guidance.30_to_50: Play carefully — avoid elites without potions, consider resting
hp_threshold_guidance.below_30: Play defensively — rest at every campfire, take the safest path, use potions liberally

question_mark_strategy.description: Question mark nodes (unknown events) can provide card transforms, relics, gold, healing, card removal, or sometimes negative effects.
when_to_prioritize: When you need healing but don't want to waste a campfire resting
When you're looking for card transforms or unusual options
When hallway fights aren't giving you useful card rewards
When you have relics that benefit from events (e.g., Ssserpent Head)
when_to_avoid: When you desperately need specific card rewards (hallway fights are more reliable)
When you can't afford any negative event outcomes
When you need guaranteed combat encounters for gold or card rewards
tips: Many events are beneficial — don't fear question marks
Some events offer free card removal, which is extremely valuable
Events that offer max HP increases are almost always worth taking
Card transform events can turn bad cards into great ones (or vice versa — risk/reward)
